Consent for Participation in a Research Study

 

Study Title: Orange Juice Preferences

 

Principal Investigator: Dr. Oleg Urminsky

 

IRB Study Number: IRB20-0711

 

DESCRIPTION: We are researchers at the University of Chicago doing a research study about consumer preferences for orange juice products and shopping habits. In this study, you will be asked to make choices about information and indicate your preferences, judgments and beliefs.  Participation should take about 5-10 minutes.  

 

RISKS and BENEFITS: The risks to your participation in this online study are those associated with basic computer tasks, including boredom, fatigue, mild stress, or breach of confidentiality. The only benefit to you is the learning experience from participating in a research study.  The benefit to society is the contribution to scientific knowledge. 

 

COMPENSATION: You will be rewarded the amount you were informed when you signed up for this task upon completion of this survey.  The platform does not allow for prorated compensation.  In the event of an incomplete task, you must contact the research team and compensation will be determined based on what was completed and at the researchers' discretion.

 

PLEASE NOTE: This study contains a number of checks to make sure that participants are finishing the tasks honestly and completely.  As long as you read the instructions and complete the tasks, your task will be approved.  If you fail these checks, your task will be rejected.

 

CONFIDENTIALITY: Your Worker ID or Participant ID or any identifier will be used to distribute payment to you but will not be stored with the research data we collect from you. The participants always have the option to opt-out of research during any point in the survey. We will be collecting IP addresses for the purpose of screening out participants who take the same study more than once, and their online worker IDs in order to keep track of each participant's participation in different studies. Any reports and presentations about the findings from this study will not include your name or any other information that could identify you. We may share the data we collect in this study with other researchers doing future studies or on public platform (e.g., OSF or GitHub) – if we share your data, we will not include information that could identify you.

 

SUBJECT’S RIGHTS: Your participation is voluntary. You may stop participating at any time by closing the browser window or the program to withdraw from the study. Partial data will not be analyzed.
